newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, hoteliers oscillate.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, hoteliers oscillate.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed on Wednesday as declining issues offset slight gains among hoteliers. Traders expect further fluctuations until more money enters the market and stabilises prices.
"There is room for tourist firms to go further down," said Igor Kos of Taurus brokerage. "This trading is just sounding the market and prices on a small volume of shares."
Of five active hoteliers on Wednesday two were flat and three down.
The biggest loser was hotelier Laguna, which lost the 50 kuna it had recovered on Tuesday, to close at 1,250 kuna on a volume of 77 shares.
Arena closed 10 kuna down to close at 160 on a volume of 53 shares and Jadranturist lost five kuna to close at 280 on 50 shares.
Riviera and Suncani Hvar remained flat.
"This small trading will continue until investors make up their mind and buy a larger portion of shares," Kos said.
For the last two weeks the volume, except for top listings Zagrebacka Banka, remained exceptionally small, with even the most popular issues trading in double-digit figures.
Of six other active issues another one was down, four were up and fully listed drug firms Pliva closed flat at 13,500 kuna on volume of 82 shares.
Volume was down at 6247 shares but the value of trades was up at 5.7 million kuna, thanks mainly trading in Zagrebacka Banka.
Zagrebacka was the most actively traded stock, closing 15 kuna down at 980, on volume of 4,022.
Kos said the blue chips, both of which are traded in London as well, would retain the same price, oscilating "within a ten percent range."
The biggest gainer in Wednesday's trading was shipper Jadroplov which rose 35 kuna to close at 250 on a volume of 20 shares.
Electric manufacturer Koncar, listed on the Zagreb bourse for the first time on Monday, gained 30 kuna to close at 410 on volume of 100 shares.
